newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China's Jiang welcome to Taiwan anytime, says Lee.
newsitem.headline: China's Jiang welcome to Taiwan anytime, says Lee.

text.p: Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui on Sunday renewed an invitation to China's leader, saying his mainland counterpart was welcome to visit the island "anytime".
"I would like to make a trip of peace to the mainland and hold a meeting with communist China's leader," Lee said when meeting a group of visiting U.S. senators in Taipei.
"If communist China's leader wants to visit Taiwan, I'll personally welcome him anytime," the official Central News Agency quoted Lee as telling the U.S. senators.

Lee has repeatedly called for a meeting with Jiang Zemin, but his latest call was denied when the Philippines, which is hosting the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit next week, rejected Taiwan's request that Lee be allowed to attend the along with Jiang.
China regards Taiwan as a Chinese province not entitled to foreign ties since a civil war separated them in 1949. Both governments say they want reunification, but under very different terms.
The latest political impasse between Taiwan and China started in June 1995 after Lee made a private visit to the United States, which Beijing saw as a move to promote independence.
After Lee's U.S. visit, Beijing suspended semi-official talks with Taipei and launched its campaign of military intimidation, which peaked ahead of Taiwan's presidential election on March 23.
